requirement_text.ISS-0216: Letflow.Api.Pagination.decode_cursor/4 trusts its caller-supplied prefix with no non-empty guard, a real bypass path once REQ-072-onward endpoints call it. check_prefix/2 (lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex) uses a size guard (byte_size(decoded) >= byte_size(prefix) and String.starts_with?(decoded, prefix)) that trivially passes if prefix is an empty string, since every decoded cursor starts with the empty string -- an empty prefix defeats the cross-endpoint isolation this parameter exists to provide. Filed 2026-08-21 as unreachable-but-real-risk (REQ-072 routing layer was pending); NOW LIVE -- confirmed 2026-08-26 that real route handlers (lib/letflow/routers/audit.ex, tasks.ex, instances.ex, routers/tenants.ex, routers/identity.ex, definitions.ex) already call decode_cursor/4 with hardcoded non-empty module-attribute prefixes. The guard itself is still missing.

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 (registry lookup): grepped docs/issues/*.yaml for 'lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex' (affected_files field) and separately for 'prefix'/'pagination'/'check_prefix'/'cursor' across every resolved-or-not entry. Only ISS-0216 itself references lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex in affected_files -- no other docs/issues/*.yaml entry, resolved or otherwise, addresses this module or the check_prefix/2 empty-string bypass. This is a fresh diagnosis of an issue already on record as open, not a recurrence of a previously-resolved fix that failed to hold -- severity stays at the filed MINOR pending this run's own assessment (see below on why MINOR may need revisiting once CODE-DESIGNER scopes the fix, since the finding note below argues the live risk is now closer to the boundary of MAJOR given confirmed reachability).

STEP 1 (diagnose):

Reproduction (real, executed via `MIX_ENV=test mix run --no-start <script>` -- this module has no Plug.Conn/Ecto.Repo dependency per its own moduledoc, so no DB connection was needed and the shared-dev-DB guard in lib/letflow/repo.ex was correctly avoided rather than bypassed):

  raw = Letflow.Api.Pagination.build_raw_cursor("T:", System.system_time(:microsecond), "abc123")
  encoded = Letflow.Api.Pagination.encode_cursor(raw)
  Letflow.Api.Pagination.decode_cursor(encoded, "", 2)

Actual output:
  encoded cursor minted under prefix "T:": VDoxNzg3NzQ1NTM5MDQ3MTA0OmFiYzEyMw
  decode with empty prefix (should be rejected, is it?): {:ok, %Letflow.Api.Pagination.Cursor{inner: "T:1787745539047104:abc123"}}
  decode with wrong non-empty prefix "X:" (expect :wrong_endpoint): {:error, :wrong_endpoint}
  decode with correct prefix "T:" (expect :ok): {:ok, %Letflow.Api.Pagination.Cursor{inner: "T:1787745539047104:abc123"}}

Confirms the bug report's claim exactly: a cursor minted under prefix "T:" and submitted with prefix "" decodes successfully ({:ok, ...}) instead of being rejected. The same cursor correctly returns {:error, :wrong_endpoint} against an unrelated non-empty prefix "X:", proving the guard mechanism works for non-empty mismatches -- the defect is specific to the empty-prefix case.

Root cause, exact function/line. lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex:211-218, private function check_prefix/2:

  defp check_prefix(decoded, prefix) do
    if byte_size(decoded) >= byte_size(prefix) and String.starts_with?(decoded, prefix) do
      :ok
    else
      {:error, :wrong_endpoint}
    end
  end

When prefix is "", byte_size(prefix) == 0, so byte_size(decoded) >= 0 is true for every decoded binary, and String.starts_with?(decoded, "") is true unconditionally per Elixir's own String.starts_with?/2 semantics (every string starts with the empty string). Both conjuncts of the guard pass regardless of decoded's actual content, so check_prefix/2 returns :ok for ANY decoded payload when prefix is "" -- the cross-endpoint isolation decode_cursor/4's own moduledoc (lines 174-177) documents this function as providing is completely defeated. This is a missing precondition, not a logic-order bug: the function has no check anywhere that prefix itself is a non-empty binary before running the size/prefix-match test.

Why no existing test caught it: grepped for a pagination test file -- test/letflow/api/pagination_test.exs exists and (per REQ-067's design) tests decode_cursor/4 with realistic non-empty prefixes exercising :ok, :wrong_endpoint, :expired, :invalid_cursor, :invalid_base64. No test in that suite calls decode_cursor/4 or check_prefix/2 with prefix "" specifically -- the empty-prefix case is an edge case only visible in the {prefix: ""} input, which the existing behavioral tests never construct because production callers are documented as always supplying a non-empty per-endpoint literal, so the test suite's authors (correctly, per REQ-067's own scope) never had a reason to test a caller contract violation that had no real caller yet. That gap is exactly the pre-REQ-072 unreachability SECURITY-REVIEWER noted in the original filing.

Call-site audit -- every current caller confirmed via grep (`grep -rn 'decode_cursor(' lib/letflow`) and each one's prefix argument traced to its declaration:

  lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex:301  -> @users_cursor_prefix = "U:" (module attribute, hardcoded literal)
  lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex:551-554 -> @group_members_cursor_prefix = "G:" (module attribute, hardcoded literal)
  lib/letflow/routers/tenants.ex:288  -> @tenants_cursor_prefix = "T:" (module attribute, hardcoded literal)
  lib/letflow/routers/audit.ex:225   -> @audit_cursor_prefix = "A:" (module attribute, hardcoded literal)
  lib/letflow/tasks.ex:653            -> @list_cursor_prefix = "T:" (module attribute, hardcoded literal)
  lib/letflow/instances.ex:260        -> @list_cursor_prefix = "IL:" (module attribute, hardcoded literal)
  lib/letflow/instances.ex:321 (via decode_seq_cursor/2, private) -> traced up one more level: decode_seq_cursor/2 is called only from lib/letflow/instances.ex:133 and :170 with @history_cursor_prefix = "IH:" and @timeline_cursor_prefix = "IT:" respectively -- both hardcoded literals, not caller/request-supplied
  lib/letflow/definitions.ex:1909-1912 -> @definitions_list_cursor_prefix = "DL:" (module attribute, hardcoded literal)
  lib/letflow/definitions.ex:2077-2080 -> @definitions_search_cursor_prefix = "DS:" (module attribute, hardcoded literal)

Every one of the 9 real call sites passes a compile-time, non-empty, module-attribute string literal as prefix -- none derive prefix from request/query/path/header input, and none pass an empty string. So today's system is NOT actively exploitable through any currently-shipped route: the risk remains latent rather than triggered by any existing endpoint. It is 'live' in the narrower sense the issue's own updated description states -- real route handlers now exist and call the vulnerable function (closing the 'no caller exists yet' gap that justified filing this MINOR/unreachable in the first place) -- but no caller today actually supplies an empty prefix, so there is no currently-reachable HTTP request that trips this bug. The exposure is: any future call site (a new endpoint, a refactor that derives prefix from a variable, or a request-context parameter per REQ-072) that fails to hard-code a non-empty literal would silently defeat cross-endpoint cursor isolation with no compiler or runtime signal, and the module's own INV-1/INV-5 doc block gives a false sense that this is structurally enforced when in fact it is only conventionally enforced by every caller currently choosing non-empty literals.

What a fix needs to change: check_prefix/2 (or decode_cursor/4 before delegating to it) needs an explicit non-empty-prefix precondition -- e.g. reject prefix == "" (and arguably any prefix that is not a binary, though the @spec already types it as String.t()) with a distinct error atom (or folding into the existing :wrong_endpoint/:invalid_cursor vocabulary -- CODE-DESIGNER's call) rather than silently returning :ok. This is a design decision (new error atom vs. reuse, and whether to add an assertion in decode_cursor/4 vs. purely in check_prefix/2) intentionally left to CODE-DESIGNER; this diagnosis only establishes that the guard is structurally absent and where.

Files read/inspected in full: docs/issues/ISS-0216.yaml, lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex, lib/letflow/routers/audit.ex, tasks.ex, instances.ex, routers/tenants.ex, routers/identity.ex, definitions.ex (grep'd for decode_cursor/decode_seq_cursor call sites and their prefix declarations). No fix implemented; no file outside handoffs/ was modified by this step.
